title: Choice Frictions in Large Assortments
eligible_reason: Treatment is continuous: every reduced-form regression uses rest_ct (number of restaurants, in 100s, available to the tract/diner at time t) or decompositions of it (var_ct cuisines, chain_ct/indep_ct, rel_ct/irrel_ct, hi/med/lo Yelp tiers) as a count regressor with diner (or tract) FE and neighborhood x time FE. No binary adoption indicator exists. Also the package data are simulated (README: 'Data used in the paper are proprietary; this replication package simulates data').
design_notes: R (lfe::felm) code. combined_reg_tables.R produces Table 2 (adoption_rate, churn_rate ~ rest_ct [+ var_ct] | tract + neighborhood_time; order_ct, spending ~ rest_ct [+ var_ct] | diner_id_f + neighborhood_time; cluster neighborhood_time) and Figure 1 (effects of a 1-SD increase in entry). panel_effect_by_rest_type.R (Tables 3, 5), panel_effect_on_order_characteristics.R (Table 4), panel_search_regressions.R (Tables 6-7), panel_interpurchase_times.R (Table 8). Sim folder generates adopt_panel.csv and cust_panel.csv.gz from Par_Draws.csv.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Not applicable: continuous exposure (restaurant count) rather than a binary adoption event.

specs.treatment_definition: number of restaurants delivering to the diner's location at time t (continuous)
specs.notes: Representative of all specs in the package.

data_files: Replication packet/data/Par_Draws.csv (parameter draws used to simulate data; analysis panels must be generated by sim/*.R)
screener_notes: Sun-Abraham / de Chaisemartin flags in the full text likely refer to discussion only; no such estimator appears in the code.
